subject: Geopolitics
title: NATO Expansion Debate
description: A short lesson to help you apply NATO Expansion Debate.

hook.text: In 1990 NATO had 16 members. By 2024 it had 32. Russia watched its buffer zone evaporate country by country.

buildup.text: Former Soviet satellites — Poland, the Baltics, Romania — all joined NATO seeking protection from Moscow.

discovery.text: Russia views NATO expansion as a broken promise and an existential threat on its doorstep.

twist.text: Western leaders argue no promise was made. Each nation chose freely. The two sides remember 1990 differently.

climax.text: This dispute fuels every Russia–West crisis: Georgia 2008, Crimea 2014, Ukraine 2022. The wound never healed.

punchline.text: Security for one side became insecurity for the other.

quiz.question: How does Russia view NATO expansion?
options: As a positive sign of European democracy
As a broken promise and existential threat
As irrelevant to its security interests
